name: Modifying a List (Case 2)
description: Construct a program that swaps pairs of adjacent elements of the list. For example, if the list is [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], the program will change it to [2, 1, 4, 3, 6, 5].\nThis program assumes that the list has always an even number of elements.
code:
#Step 1: Define and initialize the list
lst = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
#Step 2: Iterate through the pairs of adjacent elements in the list
for i in range(0, len(lst), 2):
    #Step 2.1: Swap the element at index i with the element at index i+1
    temp = lst[i]
    lst[i] = lst[i+1]
    lst[i+1] = temp
#Step 3: Print the list
print(lst)

comments.content: We define a list referred by variable lst to hold the specified numbers. We initialize the list by separating elements with a comma and enclosing the collection in square brackets [ ].

We want to iterate through pairs of the adjacent elements in the list. To really change the list as we march across it, we need to use indexes so we can assign an updated value to each position as we go.

We need the list indexes to start at 0 with every second integer number up to but not including the list length. We get this sequence by calling the range(0,len(lst),2) function.

The function len(lst) returns the number of the values in the list. The last number in the range function specifies how much to increase each successive integer in the sequence, if this is omitted then step defaults to 1. We set the step to 2 because in each iteration of the loop, we process a pair of adjacent element in the list. To move to the next pair, we need to increase the index i by 2.
Note that all statements inside the loop need to be indented with respect to the loop header.

This statement stores the value of the element at index i of the list in the temporary variable temp. Later, we use variable temp to copy the content of the element at index i into the element at the index i+1.
This statement copies the value of the element at index i+1 of the list into the element at the index i of the list.
This statement copies the value of the element at index i that we stored in temporary variable temp into the element at index i+1 of the list.
We can see the content of the list by calling the print function and passing the list to that. This statement prints the list.
